- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 3–4% after a spike, unless sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.2–0.7), model shows mean-reversion bias — adjust forecast downward slightly (−0.5 to −1.5%) to align with historical mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true outcome by 1–3 days — if sentiment is trending, shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to capture momentum.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversals” (e.g., +0.8 → -0.7 → +0.5), model fails to adjust — apply smoothing filter to reduce abrupt swings in forecast.
- If last 3–5 days of sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.2), model tends to underestimate — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for suppressed sentiment.
